I can reproduce with `v0.10.4`. On `nightly`, the snippet works fine.

I don't have `emmet_ls` installed. So I copied the relevant code in your `minitest.zip` to an `init.lua` I used earlier:

<details>

<summary>init.lua</summary>

```lua
---@diagnostic disable: undefined-global
local function setup_deps(path_to_site)
  local mini_path = path_to_site .. "pack/deps/start/mini.nvim"
  if not vim.uv.fs_stat(mini_path) then
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local clone_cmd = { "git", "clone", "--filter=blob:none", "https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim", mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd("packadd mini.nvim | helptags ALL")
    vim.cmd('echo "Installed `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
  end
  require("mini.deps").setup({ path = { package = path_to_site } })
end
setup_deps(vim.fn.stdpath("data") .. "/site/")

vim.g.mapleader = " "
MiniDeps.now(function()
  require("mini.icons").setup()
  require("mini.snippets").setup() -- only using lsp snippets
  require("mini.completion").setup()

  MiniDeps.add("williamboman/mason.nvim")
  MiniDeps.add("williamboman/mason-lspconfig.nvim")
  MiniDeps.add("neovim/nvim-lspconfig")
  require("mason").setup()
  require("mason-lspconfig").setup({ ensure_installed = { "emmet_ls" } })

  local capabilities = vim.lsp.protocol.make_client_capabilities()
  capabilities.textDocument.completion.completionItem.snippetSupport = true
  require("lspconfig").emmet_ls.setup({
    -- on_attach = function(_, buf_id) vim.bo[buf_id].omnifunc = "v:lua.MiniCompletion.completefunc_lsp" end,
    capabilities = capabilities,
    filetypes = { "css", "html", "javascript" },
  })
end)

```
</details>

On v0.10.4, the resolved on line 1122 is:

{
  error = {
    code = -32601,
    message = "Unhandled method completionItem/resolve",
    <metatable> = {
      __tostring = <function 1>
    }
  }
}

On nightly, that same resolved is:

{
  err = <1>{
    code = -32601,
    message = "Unhandled method completionItem/resolve",
    <metatable> = {
      __tostring = <function 1>
    }
  },
  error = <table 1>
}

As there is no err key on v0.10.4, on line 1123 the value becomes resolved.result, which is nil.

@echasnovski, shall I write a PR?

EDIT:

See lsp.lua in Neovim from this commit on 20241024:

-- The error key is deprecated and will be removed in 0.13
results[ctx.client_id] = { err = err, error = err, result = result }

reply_data.body:
> EDIT:
> 
> See [lsp](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/f5714994bc4fc578b5f07bca403e7067e6d9b5a0/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L1213) in Neovim, from commit `1471dfc85964a9d95c216619d715bfe449d97c19` on 20241024:
> 
> > -- The error key is deprecated and will be removed in 0.13
> > results[ctx.client_id] = { err = err, error = err, result = result }

Yeah, that seems to be the case and [is documented as deprecated](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/f5714994bc4fc578b5f07bca403e7067e6d9b5a0/runtime/doc/deprecated.txt#L46-L47). One extra thing I was curious about is why 'mini.completion' uses `err` in the first place for similar contexts. It indeed seems to be my mistake as as far as I can see (all the way to the Neovim 0.5.1) the shape of result in `buf_request_all` is indeed a table from client id to `{ error = error, result = result }`. Probably used `err` because it was named that way as an argument in `:h lsh-handler`.

> @echasnovski, shall I write a PR?

Sure, if you'd like to. Please, use something like `x.err or x.error` in all places that it is used (there are several).

---

~There is also another issue here as 'mini.completion'  [does attempt to see](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/18520ad6bbf7e6408b8449658326dc0c947c3507/lua/mini/completion.lua#L1251) if the server supports resolving completion item. Maybe it also does that not correctly.~ Nope, everything is correct on 'mini.completion' part. It is just that `emmet_ls` has `server_capabilities.completionProvider.resolveProvider = true` while throwing this kind of `"Unhandled method completionItem/resolve"` error :facepalm: 

---

(Also, @abeldekat, a small question: is there a reason all your commits don't link to the GitHub account? Like [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/pull/1671/commits), for example. This prevents you from being listed as a contributor in 'mini.nvim' repo.)
